title: Pool of Radiance
build: version 1.0, eight D64 images (archive.org d64_Pool_of_Radiance_v1.0_1988_SSI_Disk_1_of_4_Side_A); BOOT prints "POOL OF RADIANCE, VERSION 1.0"

records.c: The icon pieces' pictures, CHARPIC00, eight bytes for each character code: the picture of piece n is at $9900 + 8n, copied into the RAM character set for each cell of a figure. Characters $00-$07: 2 arm, 2 shield, 2 leg, 1 cap, 1 body; 8 multicolour.
Character $00's picture, its second row; when GEN's directory menu builds in this buffer, the menu's column.
Character $00's picture from its third row, then characters $01-$07; when GEN's directory menu builds in this buffer, the menu's row, then the names from $9903.
Characters $08-$0F: 2 arm, 2 weapon, 1 leg, 1 shield, 1 body, 1 unused; 7 multicolour.
Characters $10-$17: 2 leg, 2 hair, 2 arm, 1 weapon, 1 body; 8 multicolour.
Characters $18-$1F: 3 arm, 2 leg, 1 weapon, 1 hair, 1 body; 8 multicolour.
Characters $20-$27: 3 unused, 1 blank, 1 arm, 1 leg, 1 body, 1 shield; 8 multicolour.
Characters $28-$2F: 3 unused, 1 weapon, 1 cap, 1 body, 1 hair, 1 leg; 8 multicolour.
Characters $30-$37: 6 unused, 1 body, 1 leg; 8 multicolour.
Characters $38-$3F: 2 leg, 2 unused, 2 arm, 1 body, 1 shield; 7 multicolour.
Characters $40-$47: 3 arm, 2 body, 1 unused, 1 weapon, 1 leg; 8 multicolour.
Characters $48-$4F: 3 arm, 2 body, 2 weapon, 1 unused; 6 multicolour.
Characters $50-$57: 4 arm, 3 unused, 1 body; 8 multicolour.
Characters $58-$5F: 5 unused, 2 arm, 1 hair; 8 multicolour.
Characters $60-$67: 4 leg, 3 arm, 1 body; 8 multicolour.
Characters $68-$6F: 5 arm, 3 unused; 8 multicolour.
Characters $70-$77: 3 body, 2 weapon, 2 arm, 1 shield; 7 multicolour.
Characters $78-$7F: 4 arm, 1 weapon, 1 unused, 1 hair, 1 body; 8 multicolour.
Characters $80-$87: 3 body, 2 weapon, 1 leg, 1 hair, 1 arm; 8 multicolour.
Characters $88-$8F: 3 arm, 2 unused, 2 leg, 1 body; 8 multicolour.
Characters $90-$97: 2 leg, 2 unused, 2 body, 2 arm; 8 multicolour.
Characters $98-$9F: 3 arm, 3 body, 2 unused; 8 multicolour.
Characters $A0-$A7: 3 hair, 2 body, 1 unused, 1 cap, 1 arm; 7 multicolour.
Characters $A8-$AF: 4 arm, 2 unused, 1 hair, 1 body; 7 multicolour.
Characters $B0-$B7: 3 unused, 3 weapon, 1 leg, 1 body; 8 multicolour.
Characters $B8-$BF: 8 weapon; 7 multicolour.
Characters $C0-$C7: 3 weapon, 3 hair, 1 unused, 1 arm; 6 multicolour.
Characters $C8-$CF: 7 hair, 1 unused; 8 multicolour.
Characters $D0-$D7: 3 hair, 2 cap, 2 weapon, 1 unused; 7 multicolour.
Characters $D8-$DF: 4 weapon, 2 body, 2 leg; 7 multicolour.
Characters $E0-$E7: 4 weapon, 2 body, 2 arm; 6 multicolour.
Characters $E8-$EF: 4 weapon, 2 body, 1 arm, 1 unused; 7 multicolour.
Characters $F0-$F7: 4 unused, 3 hair, 1 arm; 7 multicolour.
Characters $F8-$FD: 5 hair, 1 unused; 4 multicolour. The file ends two bytes into character $FD, so its last two bytes, and characters $FE and $FF, are not loaded; the editor blanks $A0E9-$A0FF.
Character $FD's picture, of which the file holds the first six bytes. The editor's blanking loop (STA $A0E8,X for X = 23 down to 1) clears $A0E9-$A0FF, so this first byte stays as loaded.

For each character code, the kind of piece it draws in bits 0-6 (0 weapon, 1 body, 2 cap, 3 hair, 4 shield, 5 arm, 6 leg, the order of the COLOR menu; 7 only for $20, the blank; 15 a code no figure uses) and bit 7 set for a multicolour picture. SPELLE64 starts here. Codes $00-$3F: 15 unused, 12 arm, 12 leg, 8 body, 5 shield, 5 weapon, 4 hair, 2 cap, 1 blank.
Codes $40-$7F: 26 arm, 14 unused, 10 body, 6 weapon, 5 leg, 2 hair, 1 shield.
Codes $80-$BF: 14 arm, 13 body, 13 weapon, 12 unused, 6 leg, 5 hair, 1 cap.
Codes $C0-$FF: 21 hair, 17 weapon, 9 unused, 6 arm, 6 body, 2 cap, 2 leg, 1 type 14.
The large weapons, 35 choices: the first code of each choice's ready pose, by choice.
The large weapons: the first code of each choice's action pose.
The large weapons: the cell of the ready pose that first code goes in (cells 0-8, three by three from the top left): 0, 2, 3, 5.
The large weapons: the cell of the action pose for its first code: 2, 5.
The large weapons: for the ready pose, the number of the cell string (cell_strings) that fills the other cells in order: 1 to 22.
The large weapons: the cell string for the action pose: 24 to 42.
The large heads, 23 choices: the first code of each choice's ready pose, by choice. Bytes past the first 23 are left over: the editor never reads them.
The large heads: the first code of each choice's action pose.
The large heads: the cell of the ready pose that first code goes in (cells 0-8, three by three from the top left): 1.
The large heads: the cell of the action pose for its first code: 1.
The large heads: for the ready pose, the number of the cell string (cell_strings) that fills the other cells in order: 0 to 75.
The large heads: the cell string for the action pose: 0 to 75.
The small weapons, 28 choices: the first code of each choice's ready pose, by choice. Bytes past the first 28 are left over: the editor never reads them.
The small weapons: the first code of each choice's action pose.
The small weapons: the cell of the ready pose that first code goes in (cells 0-8, three by three from the top left): 0, 2, 3, 5.
The small weapons: the cell of the action pose for its first code: 2, 5.
The small weapons: for the ready pose, the number of the cell string (cell_strings) that fills the other cells in order: 43 to 57.
The small weapons: the cell string for the action pose: 59 to 71.
The small heads, 14 choices: the first code of each choice's ready pose, by choice. Bytes past the first 14 are left over: the editor never reads them.
The small heads: the first code of each choice's action pose.
The small heads: the cell of the ready pose that first code goes in (cells 0-8, three by three from the top left): 1.
The small heads: the cell of the action pose for its first code: 1.
The small heads: for the ready pose, the number of the cell string (cell_strings) that fills the other cells in order: 0 to 80.
The small heads: the cell string for the action pose: 0 to 80.

The cell strings, each a zero-terminated list of codes for the cells of a pose after the one its first code took, numbered from 0 here: string 0 is empty, the rest mostly eight codes. Strings 0 to 7 start in $ABC0-$ABFF.
Cell strings 8 to 15 start in $AC00-$AC3F.
Cell strings 16 to 22 start in $AC40-$AC7F.
Cell strings 23 to 30 start in $AC80-$ACBF.
Cell strings 31 to 37 start in $ACC0-$ACFF.
Cell strings 38 to 44 start in $AD00-$AD3F.
Cell strings 45 to 51 start in $AD40-$AD7F.
Cell strings 52 to 58 start in $AD80-$ADBF.
Cell strings 59 to 65 start in $ADC0-$ADFF.
Cell strings 66 to 72 start in $AE00-$AE3F.
Cell strings 73 to 82 start in $AE40-$AE59.

The icon being edited, as GEN's make_icon leaves it (from $4BE0 + 36 times the party slot): eighteen character codes, the ready pose's nine cells, three by three from the top left, then the action pose's. make_icon writes over the file's own bytes here before the call, and at EXIT the new icon goes back here.
The icon's eighteen colours, one for each cell: the piece's colour, 0 to 7, plus 8 for a multicolour piece.

The combat icon editor, which make_icon calls. Takes the figures' size from the character's $6B99 bit 0 ($B5F1: 1 for the man-sized races, 0 for dwarves, gnomes and halflings), loads CHARPIC00, the pieces' pictures, into slot 21 ($9900) and SPELLE64, their tables, into slot 7 ($A700), and blanks $A0E9-$A0FF. It marks the character set to be installed again ($6DDF), keeps the icon twice (start_icon), clears the figures' window and prints NEW over READY ACTION and OLD over READY ACTION. The background becomes dark grey ($0B, kept in $B653), text multicolour, with light red ($0A) and black as the two shared colours; then the four figures are drawn (draw_figures, X = 3).
The loop that blanks $A0E9-$A0FF counts down here.
The multicolour bit, ORed into $D016.

The menu ICON: PARTS COLOR SIZE EXIT, the highlight where it was ($B655). EXIT, or the key that leaves a menu, copies the new icon back to $AF00 (keep_new_icon), puts the background colour back and returns to GEN. SIZE runs size_menu; PARTS and COLOR run part_menu with $B5F2 = 0 or 1.

SIZE: the menu bar shows the size the figures are now, LARGE when $B5F1 is 1 and SMALL when it is 0, with EXIT. Choosing the size shown changes it to the other and shows the menu again. The size decides which weapons and heads PARTS offers; nothing writes it back to the character.
The menu bar ICON: PARTS COLOR SIZE EXIT: the item count, the heading, then each item, zero-terminated.
The menu bar SIZE: SMALL LARGE EXIT; size_menu shows one of the two sizes.
PARTS' menu bar, WEAPON HEAD EXIT, with no heading.
COLOR's menu bar, WEAPON BODY CAP HAIR SHIELD ARM LEG EXIT, the seven kinds of piece in the order of piece_types; its item texts are also editor messages 13 to 19.
Message 13: "WEAPON", also the COLOR menu's item.
Message 14: "BODY", also the COLOR menu's item.
Message 15: "CAP", also the COLOR menu's item.
Message 16: "HAIR", also the COLOR menu's item.
Message 17: "SHIELD", also the COLOR menu's item.
Message 18: "ARM", also the COLOR menu's item.
Message 19: "LEG", also the COLOR menu's item.
The two menu bars part_menu shows, two bytes each by $B5F2: parts_menu_bar, then color_menu_bar.
part_menu_bars read one byte on, for the high bytes.
The EXIT item's number in each of those menus: 2, then 7.

PARTS ($B5F2 = 0) or COLOR (1). The questions' window reads WHICH TYPE OF PART? over the menu WEAPON HEAD EXIT or WEAPON BODY CAP HAIR SHIELD ARM LEG EXIT; EXIT or the key that leaves a menu returns. Otherwise the item goes to $B5F3 and the window reads CHOOSE, the kind (HEAD, or the item's name), PART FOR or COLOR FOR, the character's name and (USE RIGHT/LEFT TO CHOOSE), with <CR>,BUTTON TO ACCEPT, <SP> TO ABORT on the bottom row. Then pick_piece or pick_color, and the menu again.
How many choices each set of pieces has, by piece_set ($B63C, the size times two plus the part): 28 small weapons, 14 small heads, 35 large weapons, 23 large heads.
Where each set's tables are in SPELLE64, two bytes each by piece_set: small_weapon_first ($A9E0), small_head_first ($AAD0), large_weapon_first ($A800), large_head_first ($A8F0).
piece_sets read one byte on, for the high bytes.

PARTS: right and left step through the set's choices. Keeps the icon now at $AF00 for an abort; the set is the size times two plus the part (piece_set), its count from piece_counts, the choice starting at 0; keeps the head's cells (save_head). On each key (read_choice_key): accept returns with the icon as it is; abort puts back the icon kept, redraws and returns; right and left step the choice, wrapping at either end, and lay it out from $B14C.

Lays out choice $B63E of the set whose tables piece_sets gives ($9E/$9F), for the ready pose and then the action pose ($B640 = 0, then 9, the choice moved on by 40). In each the first code ($9E + choice) goes in the cell the table gives ($9E + $50 + choice), and cell string number ($9E + $A0 + choice) fills the pose's other cells in order (put_piece). After both, the hair and caps the weapon left bare come back (restore_head), the new figures are drawn again, and a head's cells are kept again.
The address in the cell strings, low byte: set to $ABC0 (cell_strings) and moved on past as many strings as the table's number.
The cell string address's high byte, as the strings are skipped.
The cell string's address for the loop that lays it out, low byte, moved on with $B182.
The cell string address's high byte, as the string is laid out.

Puts code A in cell $B643 of the new icon ($B5F4) with its colour: the colour chosen for its kind ($B645 + the kind), plus 8 when piece_types marks it multicolour. A cap or hair piece (kinds 2 and 3) does not replace a piece of another kind in the top two cells of either pose (cells 0, 1, 9 and 10).
The cells save_head and restore_head keep: 0 and 1, the ready pose's top left and top middle, and 9 and 10, the action pose's.
save_head's copy of the codes in those cells.
save_head's copy of their colours.
Keeps the codes and colours of cells 0, 1, 9 and 10 (head_cells), with cells 0 and 9 blanked ($20) in the copy unless they hold hair (kind 3).
After a weapon is laid out ($B5F3 = 0): each cap or hair piece save_head kept goes back into its cell when the weapon left that cell blank ($20).

COLOR: keeps the colours now at $AF12 for an abort. On each key (read_choice_key): accept returns; abort puts the colours back, redraws and returns; right and left step the colour of the kind chosen ($B645 + $B5F3) through 0 to 7, wrapping, and every cell holding a piece of that kind takes it, plus 8 for a multicolour piece; then the new figures are drawn again.
draw_figures for the new icon's two figures (X = 1).
Draws figures X down to 0 (draw_figure): 0 and 1 the new icon's ready and action poses, 2 and 3 the old icon's.
Copies the new icon, codes and colours, to $AF00 and $AF12 for make_icon.

Draws figure $B64D: for each of its nine cells, 8 down to 0, copies the piece's picture, eight bytes from $9900 + 8 times its code, into the cell's own character of the RAM character set, $60 plus the cell's number among the 36 (with all 64 KB of RAM switched in for the copy, all_ram), then puts that character on the screen at the cell's place (figure_cells) and the cell's colour in colour RAM, $0C00 above.
The character's address in the RAM character set, low byte: set from figure_charsets and stepped down 8 for each cell.
The RAM character set address's high byte.

For cell $B64E of figure $B64D: its number among the 36 ($B64F, 9 times the figure plus the cell), its colour ($B651, from $B618 + the number, which runs on into the old icon's colours), its character ($B650 = $60 + the number), and $51/$52 pointing at the piece's picture, $9900 + 8 times its code.

Copies the icon make_icon gave into both the new icon ($B5F4, colours $B618) and the old ($B606, $B62A), and takes each kind's colour from it ($B645 + the kind). A cell whose piece is kind 15 keeps neither its colour nor the kind's.

The screen address of each of the 36 cells, two bytes each, nine to a figure in the order of the icon's cells: the new icon's ready figure at $CC7C (row 3, column 4) and action figure at $CC82 (column 10), the old icon's at $CD94 and $CD9A (row 10).
figure_cells read one byte on, for the high bytes.
The end of figure_cells: the old action figure's cell 5, high byte, and cells 6 to 8, its bottom row at $CDEA-$CDEC.
For each figure, the address of its last cell's character in the RAM character set: $D340, $D388, $D3D0 and $D418, the characters $68, $71, $7A and $83. draw_figure works down from there.
figure_charsets read one byte on, for the high bytes.
Prints editor message X at the start of the next row, the window's left edge.
Prints editor message X at the cursor.
Prints editor message X (messages_lo, messages_hi) at row A, column Y.
Two text windows, their left and right columns and top and bottom rows: columns 1-15 and rows 1-15 for the figures, then columns 1-38 and rows 17-22 for the questions.
The figures' window (windows' first), cleared, the cursor at its top left.
The questions' window (windows' second), cleared, the cursor at its top left.
Copies four bytes from the address in $B4B7/$B4B8 to the text window ($03F2-$03F5), clears it (clear_window) and homes the cursor (cursor_home).
The window's address, low byte, written by figure_window and question_window.
The window's address, high byte.

Shows the menu bar at X (low) and Y (high) with every item; $B4C7 with the items whose bits are set in A (menu_bar's masked entry). The highlight starts on $B654; waits for a menu key (get_menu_key) and keeps the item highlighted in $B654. Returns the item chosen in A, negative for the key that leaves a menu.
editor_menu's entry with the item mask already in A, which size_menu uses.
The questions' window with editor message X on its second row.
Editor message X on the bottom row: the menu window cleared, row 24, column 0.

Waits for a key or the joystick (wait_input). Cursor right, or the joystick right ($03F0 = $17), gives A = 1; cursor left or the joystick left ($1B) gives 2; RETURN or the button alone ($0F) gives 0, accept; space, or a joystick reading of $05, gives $FF, abort. Each waits a moment (delay's $2E23, X = 150) and returns carry set. Anything else returns carry clear.
The editor's messages, zero-terminated, numbered by messages_lo and messages_hi. Message 0: " PART FOR".
Message 1: " COLOR FOR".
Messages 2 to 5, which all point here: "CHOOSE ".
Message 6: "WHICH TYPE OF PART?".
Message 7: "HEAD".
Message 8: "READY ACTION".
Message 9: "OLD".
Message 10: "NEW".
Message 11: "(USE RIGHT/LEFT TO CHOOSE)".
Message 12: "<CR>,BUTTON TO ACCEPT, <SP> TO ABORT".
The editor's 20 messages' addresses, low bytes, by number: 0-12 from $B53E, 13-19 the item texts of color_menu_bar.
The messages' addresses, high bytes.
The figures' size: 1 large, 0 small; from the character's $6B99 bit 0, changed by SIZE.
Which part_menu is up: 0 PARTS, 1 COLOR.
The item chosen in part_menu: for PARTS 0 weapon and 1 head; for COLOR the kind of piece to colour, 0 weapon to 6 leg.
The new icon's eighteen codes, as icon_codes.
The old icon's codes, as make_icon gave them.
The new icon's eighteen colours, as icon_colors.
The old icon's colours.
The set of pieces PARTS steps through: the size times two plus the part, 0 small weapons, 1 small heads, 2 large weapons, 3 large heads.
How many choices the set has (piece_counts).
The choice shown, from 0; while a choice is laid out, 40 more for the action pose's bytes.
The choice, kept while $B63E is moved on for the action pose.
The pose being laid out: 0 the ready pose's cells, 9 the action pose's.
The index into the cell string being laid out.
The cell the first code went in, which the cell string passes over.
The cell being filled.
8 when the piece being placed is multicolour, else 0.
The colour of each kind of piece, 0 to 7: weapon, body, cap, hair, shield, arm, leg and the blank; taken from the icon at the start and changed by COLOR.
The figure being drawn, 3 down to 0.
The cell being drawn, 8 down to 0.
The cell's number among the 36, 9 times the figure plus the cell.
The cell's character code, $60 plus its number.
The cell's colour.
An editor message's number, kept over a call.
The background colour ($D021) as it was, put back at EXIT.
The menu item to highlight, kept from one showing to the next.
The ICON menu's last item, for the next showing.
